title: Inspect the run. Reproduce the result.

brief.prompt: Make a technical walkthrough showing how to inspect and reproduce a Workbench experiment. Focus on workflow inputs, generation settings, artifact identity and evaluation limits instead of surveying every capability.
brief.audience: ML engineers and platform engineering leads
brief.goal: Help an engineer know what evidence to inspect before reproducing a workflow.
brief.tone: Precise, practical and candid about experimental limits.

title: Inputs first.
Then inspect the output.
scenes.subtitle: Source-conditioned augmentation: preserve the input and the generated result.
scenes.narration: Start with the input and the output. For a source-conditioned augmentation, preserve both so you can inspect what changed and reproduce the experiment.

title: Keep the recipe
with the result.
scenes.subtitle: Prompt, seed, model, configuration and run evidence belong together.
scenes.narration: For generated video, keep the prompt, seed, model and configuration with the clip. A compelling output becomes useful evidence when its recipe stays available.

title: Review the artifact and its context.
scenes.subtitle: Inspect the saved video alongside recorded generation settings.
scenes.narration: Open the saved recording in Rerun. Inspect the video alongside its recorded generation settings, and trace the media back to the original run artifact.

title: A training run
is not a success claim.
scenes.subtitle: Separate experiment completion from measured task success.
scenes.narration: Inspect held-out policy evaluations before making a capability claim. This saved experiment shows no successful evaluation tasks. Use that result to guide the next iteration.

title: Choose one workflow.
Keep its evidence.
scenes.subtitle: Use the repository workflow, preserve artifacts, and verify their hashes.
scenes.narration: Choose a workflow from the repository. Preserve its configuration and artifacts, verify their hashes, and compare results against the evidence from your own run.
